title: Relay
description: Sends app or domain traffic through HTTP/3 or HTTP/2 relay servers instead of a VPN.

AllowDNSFailover.title: Allow DNS failover
AllowDNSFailover.description: If true, the device allows the relay to failover to the default system DNS resolver.

ExcludedDomains.title: Excluded domains
ExcludedDomains.description: A list of domain strings to exclude from routing through the servers in Relays. Any connection that matches a domain in the list exactly or is a subdomain of the listed domain won't use the relay server.

ExcludedFQDNs.title: Excluded FQDNs
ExcludedFQDNs.description: A list of Fully Qualified Domain Names (FQDNs) to exclude from routing through the servers contained in Relays. Any connection that matches an FQDN in the list exactly won't use the relay server. When MatchDomains is also present, any FQDN listed in the list should be a subdomain of at least one MatchDomain value, otherwise it won't have any effect.

MatchDomains.title: Match domains
MatchDomains.description:
A list of domain strings that the system uses to determine which connection to route through the servers in Relays.

Any connection that matches a domain in the list exactly or is a subdomain of the listed domain uses the relay servers, unless it matches a domain in ExcludedDomains.

If this list and MatchFQDNs are empty, the system routes traffic to all domains to the relay servers, except those that match an excluded domain or excluded FQDN.

MatchFQDNs.title: Match FQDNs
MatchFQDNs.description: A list of Fully Qualified Domain Names (FQDNs) to route through the servers contained in Relays. Any connection that matches an FQDN in the list exactly uses the relay servers. If this list and MatchDomains are empty, the system routes traffic to all domains to the relay servers, except those that match an excluded domain or excluded FQDN.

Relays.title: Relays
Relays.description: An array of dictionaries that describe one or more relay servers that the system can chain together.

AdditionalHTTPHeaderFields.title: Additional HTTP header fields
AdditionalHTTPHeaderFields.description: A dictionary that contains custom HTTP header keys and values to add to each request. The dictionary key name represents the HTTP header field name to use, and the dictionary value is the string to use as the HTTP header field value.

additionalProperties.title: ANY
additionalProperties.description: The HTTP header field value for the corresponding header field name.

HTTP2RelayURL.title: HTTP/2 relay URL
HTTP2RelayURL.description:
The URL or URI template, as defined in RFC 9298, of a relay server that's reachable using HTTP/2 and supports proxying TCP and UDP using the CONNECT method.

Each relay needs to include either HTTP2RelayURL or HTTP3RelayURL, or it can include both.

HTTP3RelayURL.title: HTTP/3 relay URL
HTTP3RelayURL.description:
The URL or URI template, as defined in RFC 9298, of a relay server that's reachable using HTTP/3 and supports proxying TCP and UDP using the CONNECT method.

Each relay needs to include either HTTP2RelayURL or HTTP3RelayURL, or it can include both.

PayloadCertificateUUID.title: Certificate UUID
PayloadCertificateUUID.description: The UUID that points to an identity certificate payload, which the system uses to authenticate the user to the relay server.

RawPublicKeys.title: Raw public keys
RawPublicKeys.description:
An array of DER-encoded raw public keys that the system uses to authenticate the server during a TLS handshake. The server needs to use one of the keys in the handshake to authenticate.

If this array is empty, the system uses the default TLS trust evaluation.

UIToggleEnabled.title: UI toggle enabled
UIToggleEnabled.description: If true, the device allows the user to disable this network relay configuration.
